title: Detect and reconcile token-count mismatches from proxy re-encoding and chunked transfer rewrites
creator: Anita Choudhury
description: Background: We have multiple field reports and internal load tests showing sporadic token-count mismatches between client-submitted payloads and the server-side tokenization results. Root-cause analysis indicates a class of cases where intermediate HTTP proxies or gateways modify the byte stream (re-encoding, recompression, chunked-transfer re-chunking, or Content-Encoding header normalization). These changes can cause the tokenizer to observe a different canonical input than the client intended, producing either under- or over-charging on the ledger. The problem is most visible for streaming uploads (chunked transfer / websocket proxies), clients that send compressed payloads (gzip/deflate), and when clients and proxies disagree on newline/whitespace normalization. This ticket scopes detection and corrective measures for proxy re-encoding / chunked transfer edge cases and defines a reconciliation flow for affected ledgers.
problem_statement: When proxies/GW mutate or re-chunk client payloads before final canonicalization, downstream tokenization sees content that no longer maps deterministically to the original bytes. Existing metering assumes canonical decoding at ingestion which breaks when mutating intermediaries change content-encoding or chunk framing. Outcome: customers receive inconsistent invoice quantities versus what their client-side token counters expect; internal accounting shows mismatched ledgers and manual refunds.
observed_examples: Client A uploads a gzip-compressed prompt via chunked HTTP POST. A corporate proxy strips the Content-Length and re-chunks frames; server decompresses and tokenizes and reports 14% more tokens than the client estimates.

Websocket clients behind a CDN that normalizes UTF line endings. Server tokenizer treats CRLF->LF conversion differently than client library which results in off-by-1k token drifts on some long-stream sessions.
Proxy double-decompression: client sends gzip, proxy transparently decompresses for inspection and re-compresses with different metadata leading to different byte sequences seen by server tokenizer.
proposed_solution: 1) Harden ingestion: perform deterministic canonicalization as early as possible in the ingress path (explicit canonical-decoder middleware that enforces UTF-8 normalization, newline normalization, and a single agreed decompression step). 2) Preserve original payload fingerprint: compute a lightweight canonical checksum (e.g., SHA256 of canonicalized bytes) and record both original client-reported content-encoding headers and final canonicalization steps into the request manifest. 3) Metering ledger change: record token attribution tied to the request-manifest fingerprint so reconciliation can detect mismatches between client-provided checksum and server-seen checksum. 4) Reconciliation flow: when mismatch detected, run a verification job to replay canonicalization under controlled decoder flags to determine inflation/deflation factor and then apply retro-credit/debit with audit trail. 5) Monitoring and alerting: emit mismatch-rate metric, and auto-flag tenants above threshold for manual review.
design_decision_notes: We considered a client-side signed-length header to force exact byte accounting but rejected because many legacy clients and third-party proxies will strip or rewrite headers. Instead we rely on server-side canonical fingerprinting plus a client-reported optional checksum to improve attribution when present.
implementation_tasks: Add canonicalization middleware in edge ingestion (HTTP + WS). Ensure deterministic UTF-8 decode, CRLF->LF normalization, and single decompression pass.
Record request-manifest with: original content-encoding, observed content-encoding, canonical checksum, and canonicalization steps into the request trace header (opaque id).
Extend metering ledger schema to include request-manifest-id and checksum for each billed entry.
Build a reconciliation worker that can re-run canonicalization permutations (e.g., with/without proxy-aware decompression) to estimate delta and issue credits/debits.
Create unit/integration tests simulating proxy rewrite behaviors (re-chunking, header stripping, double-decompress).
Add end-to-end tests using our proxy-sim harness and synthetic clients to validate token parity.
Add Grafana dashboards and an alert for mismatch-rate > 0.05% over 24h per-tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Canonicalization middleware deployed behind a feature flag and covered by unit tests.
Metering ledger accepts request-manifest-id and can produce an evidence bundle for any billed request.
Reconciliation worker can detect and correct mismatches in synthetic repros with >95% accuracy in test harness.
Mismatch-rate alert firing threshold and dashboard created; baseline measured for 2 weeks after rollout and reduction target achieved (>=90% reduction in noisy cases).
At least one real customer case successfully reconciled and a small audit refund issued by the flow (manual approval gated).
test_plan: Unit tests: tokenizer invariants after canonicalization with permutations of newline and decompression flags.
Integration tests: proxy-sim harness that rewrites chunking and content-encoding; validate ledger attribution and reconciliation.
Performance tests: ensure canonicalization middleware adds <0.5ms median latency on hot-path for non-compressed requests and <3ms for compressed requests under p95 loads.
Chaos tests: run randomized chunks and gzip metadata rewraps; assert reconciliation worker finds consistent attribution.
Audit tests: generate evidence bundles for 1000 synthetic billing events and verify they match expected checksums.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy canonicalization middleware and manifest recording behind feature-flag to 2 internal regions and route 5% of traffic for 72h.
Phase 2 (tenant pilot): Enable for internal customers and opt-in tenants; run reconciliation worker in dry-run mode to collect evidence and compute expected credits.
Phase 3 (wide rollout): Enable manifest recording for all tenants and enable reconciliation job for low-risk mismatches (auto-credit below threshold), manual review for >$100 adjustments.
Phase 4: Post-rollout monitoring for 30 days, then remove feature flag if stable and update billing docs.
monitoring_metrics: metering.proxy_mismatch_rate: percentage of billed requests where client_checksum != server_checksum
metering.proxy_mismatch_tokens: absolute token delta attributed to proxy-mismatch per-hour
latency.canonicalization_ms: p50/p95/p99 latencies added by middleware
reconciliation.success_rate: percent of mismatches successfully reconciled in dry-run

notes: Do not conflate this work with general streaming idempotency fixes — focus strictly on content-encoding and chunking-induced drift.
Long-term: consider a client SDK feature that emits a signed canonical checksum; out-of-scope for this ticket but tracked in roadmap.
Coordinate with legal/billing before auto-crediting customers; keep manual review for large adjustments.
